kaps_punt: Persoonlik, daaglikse gebruike wat water besoedel; Fabriek en plaasafval; Afvalwater en hersirkulering van rioolvuil

items.bewering: Elke dag gebruik ons water om onsself en ons klere en skottelgoed te was.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: Department of Water Affairs and Forestry, 'Working towards a clean and healthy community' (dws.gov.za/Projects/Dense/docs/Awareness Materials/English.pdf), p. 4: 'We need it for drinking, cooking, washing and sanitation.' City of Cape Town, 'Safe Use of Greywater' (resource.capetown.gov.za): greywater is water used for washing dishes, laundering clothes and bathing. Stel-toets: 'ons' is mense saam; die sin se nie dat elke persoon elke dag klere was nie, so daar is geen 'alle/altyd'-bewering nie.

items.bewering: Seep en olie spoel dan saam met die water by die drein af.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: City of Cape Town, 'Safe Use of Greywater' (resource.capetown.gov.za) and published greywater guidance: greywater carries soap and detergent residue, oil and grease; kitchen water carries cooking oils, grease and detergents.

items.bewering: Rommel soos papier en plastieksakke waai of spoel soms tot in 'n rivier.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: DWAF booklet (dws.gov.za, as above), p. 6: solid waste is 'litter and old food dropped in the streets, or household rubbish which is thrown into the street or river'; stormwater 'washes soil, litter and other waste material into the river and streams'. UCT research (Chitaka, open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/32362) quantifies plastic litter carried into Table Bay by Cape Town's urban runoff. 'soms' is the correct hedge.

items.bewering: Water raak besoedel wanneer seep, olie, rommel of ander afval daarin beland.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: DWAF booklet (dws.gov.za, as above), p. 5, Box 1: 'Water pollution happens when the waste we produce as part of our everyday life gets into water'; p. 6 names chemicals in washing water and solid waste as pollution.

items.bewering: Chemikalieë is stowwe wat mense gebruik om dinge skoon te maak of om produkte in fabrieke te maak.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster (noun 'chemical': 'a substance obtained by a chemical process or producing a chemical effect'); in everyday use the word means manufactured or industrial substances, not substances defined by two uses. Universiteit van die Vrystaat, PUO-tesourus (pokello.ufs.ac.za/s/PUO/item/31131): kunsmis = 'chemical compounds used to increase crop yields by supplementing soil with essential nutrients'. EPA (FIFRA s. 2(u)): pesticides are substances that prevent, destroy, repel or mitigate pests.
items.regstelling: Die sin is 'n omskrywing ('Chemikalieë is ...') met 'n geslote lys van twee gebruike, en die les se eie voorbeelde val buite die lys: die volgende sin noem plaagdoders as chemikalieë, en hulle word nie gebruik om skoon te maak of om fabrieksprodukte te maak nie; en kunsmis, wat die les in 'Afval van fabrieke en plase' as plaasbesoedeling noem, is self 'n chemikalie (UV-tesourus) maar pas in geen gebruik in die lys nie. 'n Leerder wat gevra word of kunsmis 'n chemikalie is, sal volgens hierdie omskrywing 'nee' antwoord. Omskryf chemikalieë deur wat hulle IS (stowwe wat mense maak of gebruik, dikwels in fabrieke gemaak) en gee die gebruike as voorbeelde eerder as as die omskrywing self, sodat skoonmaakmiddels, plaagdoders en kunsmis almal daarin pas. Laat hierdie sin en die begrip 'chemikalieë' dieselfde ding se; tans gee die studieblok twee gebruike en die begrip drie.

items.bewering: Boere gebruik chemikalieë soos plaagdoders om hul plante teen plae te beskerm.
items.bron: US EPA, 'What is a pesticide?' (epa.gov minimum-risk-pesticides): any substance intended for preventing, destroying, repelling or mitigating any pest. Stel-toets: 'Boere' is generies, nie 'alle boere' nie, en 'soos' hou die lys oop.

items.bewering: Baie chemikalieë is nuttig, maar hulle kan water besoedel as hulle daarin beland.
items.bron: US EPA agricultural runoff fact sheet and 'Basic information about nonpoint source pollution' (epa.gov/nps): pesticides and excess fertilisers are among the pollutants runoff carries into rivers and lakes. DWAF booklet p. 6: chemicals in washing water can make people and animals sick. 'kan' is the correct hedge.

items.bewering: Bakterieë is piepklein lewende organismes wat jy nie met die blote oog kan sien nie.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'bacteria': 'any of a group of microscopic single-celled organisms'. DWAF booklet p. 6: 'Tiny living creatures, such as germs ... Although we can't see these things, they can make humans and animals very sick.' VIR 'n MENS OM TE WEET, nie 'n bevinding nie: daar is skaars reuse-uitsonderings. Thiomargarita magnifica (beskryf in Science, Junie 2022; US DOE Joint Genome Institute, jgi.doe.gov) is omtrent 1 cm lank en met die blote oog sigbaar, en Thiomargarita namibiensis van die Namibiese kus is byna sigbaar. Naslaanwerke omskryf bakterieë steeds as mikroskopies, dus aanvaar op Graad 4; 'n veiliger vorm sou 'die meeste bakterieë' wees, as 'n mens dit verkies.

items.bewering: Sommige bakterieë in water is onskadelik, maar ander kan mense en diere siek maak.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: DWAF booklet p. 6: dirty washing water 'contains bacteria, or small organisms that can make us sick'; sewage 'has bacteria that can make us sick'. Britannica: most bacteria are harmless or beneficial, so 'sommige' onderskat maar is nie vals nie.

items.bewering: Helder water kan dus steeds bakterieë bevat wat mense siek kan maak.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: CDC press release, 14 March 2005 (archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/media/pressrel/r050314.htm): water 'that appears to be clean but may harbor these infectious organisms', naming Shigella and E. coli O157:H7 among them. Nelson Mandela Bay, February 2022 (HeraldLIVE / TimesLIVE): residents told to boil municipal tap water after microbiological limits were exceeded.

items.bewering: Fabrieke gebruik water om produkte te maak en hul afvalwater kan chemikalieë bevat.
items.bron: DWAF booklet p. 4: water 'is needed in mining, industry and agriculture'. GroundUp, 'Pollution is killing Gauteng's fresh water sources' (groundup.news, 2026): Gauteng rivers carry 'industrial waste and toxic chemicals'. Stel-toets: 'kan' - fabrieke word nie as klas vuil voorgestel nie.

items.bewering: Boere gebruik kunsmis om hul gewasse beter te laat groei.
items.bron: Universiteit van die Vrystaat, PUO-tesourus (pokello.ufs.ac.za/s/PUO/item/31131): kunsmis is used 'to increase crop yields by supplementing soil with essential nutrients'. IFDC and Fertilizer Australia: fertilisers supply nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium so crops grow larger and healthier.

items.bewering: Reën kan kunsmis en plaagdoders van die lande af in 'n rivier of 'n dam spoel.
items.bron: US EPA, 'Basic information about nonpoint source pollution' (epa.gov/nps): runoff from rainfall picks up pollutants and deposits them in lakes, rivers and wetlands, including 'excess fertilizers, herbicides and insecticides from agricultural lands'; EPA agricultural runoff fact sheet.

items.bewering: Kunsmis, plaagdoders en afvalwater kan die water in riviere en damme besoedel.
items.bron: US EPA nonpoint-source pages (as above); GroundUp 2026 (as above) on Gauteng rivers and the Vaal and Hartbeespoort dams. Stel-toets oor die hele les: elke bron (huise, fabrieke, plase) word met 'kan' of 'soms' as moontlike besoedelaar gestel; geen bron word as klas vuil voorgestel nie, en daar is geen 'alle', 'altyd' of 'nooit' nie.

items.bewering: Besoedeling van huise en fabrieke en plase kan stroomaf vloei na mense en diere verder langs die rivier.
items.bron: DWAF booklet p. 3: 'The waste that one settlement allows to get into water flows downstream to affect people in other settlements'; p. 4: 'the next community living along the river is going to be getting polluted water ... all down the river.'

items.bewering: Riool is die vuil water en menslike afval wat uit huise, skole en ander geboue weggevoer word.
items.bron: Meaning: sewage is the wastewater, including human waste, carried from homes and other buildings (EPA: sewers collect sewage and wastewater from homes, businesses and industries). Afrikaans usage: Oudtshoorn Courant, 'Riool beland in Grobbelaarsrivier' (2018) uses 'riool' for the waste itself ('Rou riool wat in die Grobbelaarsrivier beland', 'Al Oudtshoorn se riool vloei na die watersuiweringswerke') and separately 'rioolpyp' for the pipe; Graaff-Reinet Advertiser and Suidkaap Forum likewise. Note: Afrikaans Wiktionary gives only the pipe sense, so both senses are in use; the lesson's sense is the one South African Afrikaans press uses.

items.bewering: In dorpe en stede loop baie van die riool deur pype na 'n rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg.
items.bron: Stats SA census and General Household Survey data (via SAnews/Africa Check): flush toilets connected to the public sewerage system are most common in the most urbanised provinces (Western Cape 89.1%, Gauteng 88.6%); 57% of households nationally in 2011. 'baie van' is the correct hedge - not all of it.

items.bewering: Daar word die vuil water skoongemaak voordat dit terug na 'n rivier of 'n ander waterbron gaan.
items.bron: As a description of what a treatment works is FOR: Wikipedia 'Secondary treatment' and City of Cape Town works descriptions (treated effluent is discharged to the river or reused for irrigation). VIR 'n MENS OM TE WEET: in Suid-Afrika slaag baie aanlegte nie daarin nie. Green Drop 2022 (DWS; Daily Maverick / GroundUp, 21 June 2022): 334 of 850 municipal works (39%) in a critical state; Afrikaans local press reports raw sewage entering the Groot-Vis at Cradock and the Grobbelaars at Oudtshoorn. The sentence describes the plant's job and is true of that; a learner in such a town might read it as a promise. Not marked as an error because the lesson does not claim every plant succeeds.

items.bewering: Gewoonlik vang groot siwwe eers rommel soos plastiek en lappe uit die water.
items.bron: Screening is the first step of preliminary treatment and removes large solids such as rags, sticks and plastic items (waterandwastewater.com, 'What is removed during primary wastewater treatment'; Engineering News on Cape Town's Zandvliet works: raw sewage is screened and the solids removed). Mapping of 'siwwe': bar and fine screens hold back large objects and let water through, as a sieve does; the mapping holds. 'Gewoonlik' correctly hedges the sequence.

items.bewering: In groot tenks sak die swaar vuiligheid daarna stadig na die bodem.
items.bron: Primary sedimentation: heavy solids sink to the bottom of large tanks and form sludge, removing 50-65% of suspended solids (waterandwastewater.com, 'What happens during primary wastewater treatment'; NBCUA). Stel-toets: not every plant has primary settling tanks (some go from screening and grit removal straight to the biological reactor), but grit channels still let heavy material settle, and the block opens on 'Gewoonlik', so the sequence does not claim every plant works the same way.

items.bewering: Nuttige bakterieë eet dan baie van die vuiligheid wat nog in die water oorbly.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Secondary treatment': 'Bacteria and protozoa consume biodegradable soluble organic contaminants (e.g. sugars, fats ... from human waste, food waste, soaps and detergent)'; activated sludge removes about 85% of organic matter. Mapping of 'eet': the bacteria take up the organic matter as food and grow on it, so the verb maps correctly; 'baie van' correctly avoids 'all'. Omission noted, not an error: most plants also settle the water again and disinfect it before release (same source).

items.bewering: Op sommige plekke word die skoongemaakte water nog verder gesuiwer en vir ander dinge hergebruik.
items.bron: Beaufort West Water Reclamation Plant, delivering since January 2011 (water360.com.au case study; Wits WIReDSpace thesis; News24 2018); eThekwini's Durban Water Recycling at the Southern Wastewater Treatment Works supplies industry (durban.gov.za water reuse brochure); Vanwyksdorp treated water irrigates sports fields (Oudtshoorn Courant 2017). 'Op sommige plekke' is the correct hedge.

items.bewering: Werkers hou die aanleg aan die gang, en die pompe en masjiene gebruik elektrisiteit.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: Workers: DWS Regulation 3630 (2023) under the Water Services Act requires registered process controllers at every water and wastewater works (PMG, Questions to the Minister of Water and Sanitation). Electricity: in a typical activated-sludge plant aeration uses about 60% and pumping about 15% of the electricity (WaterWorld, 'Energy efficiency for wastewater treatment plants'; IESO Water and Wastewater report).

items.bewering: Dit neem ook tyd om die water deur al die stappe te kry.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: Hydraulic retention time: activated-sludge aeration tanks typically hold sewage 5-8 hours and sedimentation tanks 2-4 hours (waterandwastewater.com, 'What is hydraulic retention time').

items.bewering: Al hierdie werk kos baie tyd, geld en energie.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: DWAF booklet p. 4: 'dirty water is so expensive to clean up'; p. 3: addressing pollution 'costs the country money'. Energy: WaterWorld and IESO as above (treatment plants are among a municipality's largest energy users).

items.bewering: Daarom is dit beter om water nie in die eerste plek te besoedel nie.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: DWAF booklet pp. 3-4: because dirty water is expensive to clean, 'we all have to be careful how we use it' and must stop pollution at its source. The conclusion follows from the block's own premises. 'in die eerste plek' is an idiom, not a superlative.

items.bewering: Om water, lug of grond vuil of skadelik te maak.
items.bron: Dictionary.com, 'pollute': 'to make foul or unclean, especially with harmful chemical or waste products'; standard learner sense: to damage air, water or land by putting waste or dangerous material into it. Wikidata Q58734 links Afrikaans 'besoedeling' to pollution. Read alone the entry is complete and true.

items.bewering: Stowwe wat mense gebruik om skoon te maak, produkte te maak of plante teen plae te beskerm.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, noun 'chemical' (as above); Universiteit van die Vrystaat PUO-tesourus: kunsmis = 'chemical compounds used to increase crop yields'.
items.regstelling: Alleen gelees omskryf die inskrywing chemikalieë met 'n geslote lys van drie gebruike. Kunsmis, wat die les self as plaasbesoedeling noem, is 'n chemikalie, maar dit maak nie skoon nie, is nie iets waarmee produkte gemaak word nie en beskerm nie plante teen plae nie - dit voed hulle - so die inskrywing sluit dit uit; medisyne en brandstof val ook buite. Omskryf deur wat chemikalieë IS, met die gebruike as voorbeelde, sodat die inskrywing ook kunsmis dek. Dit moet ooreenstem met die studiesin in 'Chemikalieë in water', wat tans net twee van die drie gebruike gee.

items.bewering: Piepklein lewende organismes wat jy nie met die blote oog kan sien nie. Sommige is onskadelik, maar ander kan mense en diere siek maak.
items.bron: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'bacteria' (microscopic single-celled organisms); DWAF booklet p. 6. Read alone it is true and matches the study block word for word. Same note as the study block: a few rare giant bacteria (Thiomargarita magnifica, Science 2022) are visible to the naked eye.

items.bewering: 'n Chemikalie wat gebruik word om plae soos insekte dood te maak of weg te hou.
items.bron: US EPA / FIFRA s. 2(u): a pesticide is any substance intended for 'preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest'. 'dood te maak of weg te hou' covers destroy and repel; 'soos insekte' keeps the list of pests open. Read alone it is true.

items.bewering: Water wat reeds gebruik is en daardeur vuil geword het.
items.bron: Standard definition: wastewater is 'used water from any combination of domestic, industrial, commercial or agricultural activities' (Wikipedia 'Wastewater', citing Tilley et al.). Read alone it is true at Grade 4 (the technical term also takes in stormwater and sewer infiltration, which is not a use; omission only).

items.bewering: Vuil water en menslike afval wat uit huise, skole en ander geboue weggevoer word.
items.bron: As for the study block 'Riool': the sewage sense of 'riool' is the one used in South African Afrikaans press (Oudtshoorn Courant 2018, which distinguishes 'riool' from 'rioolpyp'). Read alone it is true and matches the study block.

items.bewering: 'n Plek waar vuil rioolwater skoongemaak word voordat dit na riviere of ander waterbronne teruggaan.
items.bron: Describes a sewage treatment works correctly (Wikipedia 'Secondary treatment'; City of Cape Town works descriptions). Same note as the study block on Green Drop 2022 (39% of works critical): true of what a plant is for, not a promise about every plant. Suidkaap Forum (2023) attests the variant 'rioolsuiweringsaanleg'; the compound used here is transparent, and its form is the language checker's question, not a fact.

opsomming: Een fout, op twee plekke: die les omskryf 'chemikalieë' (in die studieblok en in die begrip, wat ook van mekaar verskil) met 'n geslote lys gebruike wat die plaagdoders van die volgende sin en die kunsmis van die les self uitsluit; al die ander 31 bewerings is bevestig - elke behandelingstap, die stel bronne (geen klas word as vuil voorgestel nie, geen alle/altyd nie, en 'Gewoonlik' dek die volgorde) en elke begrip alleen gelees - met twee voorbehoude wat 'n mens moet sien: baie Suid-Afrikaanse aanlegte maak die water in werklikheid nie skoon nie (Green Drop 2022: 39% krities), en 'n paar skaars reusebakterieë is wel met die blote oog sigbaar; die les bevat geen oortreffende trappe nie.
